title.zh: 通用释放复核，感知终态（候选 v2）

description: Version 2 of the generic release review: the same question, frames and per-opening validity as version 1, but the episode is judged by what the episode ends on. It succeeds when at least `min_valid` openings are valid, the gripper does not close again after the last valid opening (the object was not picked up again), and the last `place` time segment the live service committed for the episode (the one that starts last) is neither a failure nor unknown; no `place` time segment fails it, an unknown one makes the verdict undecided (recorded as a failure). The place condition needs the time segments and is applied by the live service, not by the review run. ONLY FOR TASKS THAT PLACE ONCE: a task that legitimately grasps again after a placement (stacking several objects) is judged a failure by this rule; use version 1 there. CANDIDATE, NOT THE DEFAULT: chosen offline on 91 scored episodes of one task (eggplant into a blue plate, one robot, one model), where it had no false success and no missed success; that is a small, single-task sample and not a measured accuracy. Written 2026-10-04; version 1 is unchanged and stays the default (`pipeline.anchored_spec`). The live page shows its verdict as automatic and unreviewed.
question:
A robot arm with a two-finger gripper is carrying out this instruction: "{task}". Work out what the instruction asks the robot to pick up and where it should end up.
The gripper receives an OPEN command at t=0; this is one release of the episode. Images 1-7 are the side camera at t=-2.5, -1.5, -0.8, -0.3, -0.1, +0.4, +1.2 s; images 8-11 are the wrist camera (looking down between the fingers) at t=-1.5, -0.6, -0.1, +0.4 s.
The gripper holds an object by pinching it, so a held object may hang tilted under the fingers; it counts as held if the whole object is off the surface it lay on and moves together with the gripper across the earlier images. An object that stays on the surface while the fingers close or drag it is NOT held.
Answer strictly from what the images show, not from what the robot seems to be trying to do:
- held_before: just before the open, is an object held off the surface by the fingers?
- landed: after the open, where is that object relative to what the instruction asks for: at_target if it rests on or in the place the instruction names as its destination; elsewhere if it rests somewhere else (the table, another object, a wrong container); still_in_gripper; nothing_released if no object was held.
- stays: at t=+1.2 s does it stay where it landed (not sliding, rolling or falling off)?
Use unclear whenever the images do not show it.
